card.head: Every robot learned it from a human hand.

lines: Every robot that can do something learned it from a human hand.

card.head: We build robots. We print the arms.
card.sub: ThenarLabs: open robot arms, the rigs that drive them, and the market that pays the people who teach them.

lines: We're ThenarLabs. We print robot arms and build the rigs that drive them, so we know how many demonstrations a single skill takes.

card.head: The people who teach robots aren't paid, and don't own the data.

lines: Robot policies learn from people driving arms through a task, over and over. Those people are rarely paid, never credited, and never own the data they made.

card.head: Physical AI is starved of demonstrations.
card.sub: Arms cheap enough to print · headsets that track your hands · agents that buy their own data

lines: And physical AI is starved of real demonstrations, just as arms got cheap enough to print, headsets learned to track hands, and AI agents started buying their own data.

card.head: Drive. Get paid. Own it.
card.sub: From a browser, a Quest or a leader arm · paid on Monad in the transaction that records the run · a share of the corpus agents buy

lines: Thenar is the market in between. Drive a robot arm from a browser, a headset or a leader arm.

notes: WEBXR · EMULATED HEADSET (IWER) · LIVE MONAD TESTNET
lines: Get paid on Monad, and own a share of the data.

card.head: 7 paid runs · 5 agent sales · 13 verified contracts
card.sub: A paid run: executed ~1 s, final ~1.2 s from the send · team-seeded, 13–14 Oct

lines: On Monad testnet, a paid run is final about a second after the send. Seven paid runs, five agent sales over x402, thirteen verified contracts: seeded by our team, and all on chain.

card.head: Operators. Labs. Agents.
card.sub: Makers and Quest owners drive · labs post bounties from a Privy budget · agents buy over x402 · reached through our open-source arms and the people who print them

lines: It's for operators, from makers to Quest owners, for labs that post bounties, and for the agents that buy the data. We reach them through our open-source arms, and the people who print them.
